LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting, part of Strand 3 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we write legibly and neatly? 2. How can you improve your handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. copy words, sentences, and paragraphs using joined letters in their books,

2. observe visuals/pictures and compose a story of about (100-120 words) in cursive script,

3. discuss the importance of writing legibly and neatly as a class,

4. team up to search for information from the internet or print sources and make notes. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. copy words, sentences, and paragraphs using joined letters in their books,
2. observe visuals/pictures and compose a story of about (100-120 words) in cursive script,
3. discuss the importance of writing legibly and neatly as a class,
4. team up to search for information from the internet or print sources and make notes. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination is developed as the learner uses visuals to write notes.

• Digital Literacy is enhanced as the learner uses internet resources to search for information on visual composition.

24

Values:
Respect is fostered as the learner accommodates diverse opinions from peers as they search for material featuring the

theme and write compositions based on the characters, places or event.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills Education - self-esteem and confidence are enhanced as the learner becomes more proficient in self- expression.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner uses legible handwriting to write texts in all learning areas as legible and neat handwriting is emphasised.
